problem.title: Length of Longest Subarray With at Most K Frequency

headline: Never Forget It: Non-Shrinking Sliding Window
problem_summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the length of the longest contiguous subarray in which every value appears at most k times.
key_insight: The window never needs to shrink back below its best-ever size: once invalid, advancing both pointers together keeps the length frozen instead of decreasing it, so the maintained length only ever grows.
intuition: Grow the window by moving end right. If a value's count exceeds k, the window is invalid, so move start right once too instead of fully repairing it. The window may stay temporarily invalid, but its length never needs to shrink below the best length already found.

naive_approach.description: Recompute frequency counts for every possible subarray.

approach: When its count becomes k + 1, increment violations.
If violations > 0, remove nums[start] and move start once.
If the removed count becomes k, decrement violations.

states: violation on third 1 -> start advances once
window length frozen, never shrinks further
example.explanation: The longest window where every value appears at most twice has length 6.

correctness: The maintained window length only grows on valid iterations; on invalid iterations both pointers move so the length stays unchanged. Therefore the final maintained length equals the largest valid length ever reached.

complexity.explanation: Each pointer moves at most n times; u is the number of unique values.

cases.label: Case 2 -- Invalid
cases.description: end moves right; start also moves right once

reasoning_panel.title: Why the final answer is n - start
bullets: Current length after processing end: end - start + 1
At the final iteration: end = n - 1
reasoning_panel.summary: The maintained window length only grows on valid iterations, so the final length is exactly the largest valid length ever reached.
